entry.name: web_search_20260318 response_inclusion:"excluded" strips raw search results from the response -- and from every later turn too
entry.reasoning: Re-fetched platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool (2026-08-20). Deciding quote, verbatim: 'The response_inclusion parameter controls how search result blocks appear in the API response when the result was consumed by a completed code execution call in the same turn. Set "response_inclusion": "excluded" to drop those nested server_tool_use and result block pairs entirely from the response... The default is "full". Results from direct calls, or from code execution calls that paused before completing, are always returned in full so they can be sent back on the next turn.' That last clause is the tell: it frames full-mode inclusion as existing 'so they can be sent back on the next turn' -- i.e. the Messages API's multi-turn contract requires echoing the previous assistant turn's content blocks back verbatim to continue a conversation. Under excluded mode the caller never receives the raw web_search_tool_result blocks, so it structurally cannot echo them back on turn N+1: the model reads a smaller, genuinely different token sequence on every later turn than it would under full mode -- exactly the bar's 'model reads different tokens' clause. This is the same shape this register already settled at entry 225 (context editing): the docs justify the feature with an outcome claim ('reducing output token costs for agentic workflows that don't need to echo raw search content back'), but the bar's own trap clause says an outcome claim never supports an identity/mechanism claim, and whether a given workflow actually needed that content later is a per-conversation fact, not a property of the feature -- the same carve-out 225 uses for its own FAIL. Difference from 225: the stripped content here is raw search results a completed code-execution call has already digested within the SAME turn, and what code extracted from them typically survives in its own separately-returned result block, so for workflows that only ever want the filtered output this is very likely harmless in practice. But 'very likely harmless in practice' is exactly the outcome-claim shape the bar excludes from earning anything above FAIL; there is no structural guarantee a later turn never needs to re-examine a specific raw source (a URL, an exact quote, a page's full text) that only existed in the dropped blocks.
entry.savings: None as an identity-preserving technique. There is a real, documented output-token reduction within the turn where it fires, but the source gives no percentage or dollar figure -- only the qualitative claim 'reducing output token costs for agentic workflows.' Any credit for that reduction is potentially offset, on some fraction of conversations, by the later-turn cost of the model no longer having access to content it might need to re-derive or ask the user to re-supply -- a cost the source does not quantify or acknowledge.
entry.provenance: Primary Anthropic docs, re-fetched directly this session via WebFetch: platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool, 'Response inclusion' section. Quote verified verbatim, including the version-gating note ('Requires web_search_20260318 or later').
entry.telemetrySignal: Content-visible, not content-blind: on a multi-turn conversation using dynamic filtering with response_inclusion="excluded", the assistant content array for the search-bearing turn is directly observable to omit server_tool_use/web_search_tool_result block pairs for searches consumed by a completed code_execution call. A pure usage-object watcher would only see a lower output_tokens count that turn and could not distinguish 'fewer searches ran' from 'results were dropped after being consumed' without reading content.
entry.verifiedAgainst: 2026-08-20: WebFetch on platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool; 'drop those nested server_tool_use and result block pairs entirely from the response' and 'always returned in full so they can be sent back on the next turn' both present verbatim.
entry.trap: The 'already consumed this turn' qualifier makes this feel safer than context editing's blunt placeholder substitution, and it likely is safer in most agentic-code-execution workflows -- but 'likely safer in most workflows' is an outcome claim, and the bar is explicit that outcome claims don't upgrade a mechanism claim. Anyone whose later turns occasionally need to point back at a specific raw source that code execution filtered out will hit exactly the failure mode entry 225 describes, with no error surfaced.
entry.settlingExperiment: Run the same two-turn dynamic-filtering conversation twice, once with response_inclusion:"full" and once "excluded"; diff the exact content sent as turn-2 conversation history to confirm the raw search-result blocks are structurally absent under excluded mode. Not required to reach this verdict (the docs' own 'sent back on the next turn' language already settles the mechanism) but would give an exact byte-count delta.
entry.implementationNote: If a workflow needs to preserve the option of referencing raw search content on a later turn, leave response_inclusion at its default ("full") and handle any output-token trimming manually -- the same caveat entry 225 already gives for context editing.

GPT-5.4/5.5: 'prompt caching is automatic: the system caches eligible prefixes of 1,024 tokens or longer without additional parameters, and cache writes are free of charge.' GPT-5.6: 'GPT-5.6 moves to the controllable model described above, including the 1.25 times cache-write rate, which applies to implicit and explicit writes alike,' where the 'controllable model' is prompt_cache_breakpoint markers on content blocks (up to 4/request, 1,024-token minimum section). AWS's own stated breakeven: 'a workload lowers its net input cost once cache reads make up roughly 20 percent of the tokens that flow through the cache' -- below that, upgrading to GPT-5.6 with heavy cache-write, low-reuse traffic is a net cost increase versus GPT-5.4/5.5.

entry.name: BatchLLM (he-yufeng) — SHA-256 checkpoint fingerprint gates crash-resume replay, verified in source not just docs
entry.reasoning: Verified directly in code, not just the README. processor.py:307-320 builds a fingerprint via `hashlib.sha256(json.dumps({"items":items,"model":...,"system_prompt":...,"prompt_template":...,"max_tokens":...,"temperature":...,"base_url":...,"max_retries":...,"timeout":...}, sort_keys=True, ...).hexdigest()`, stores it as the checkpoint's first line (`_batchllm_checkpoint`), and on load (processor.py:358-366) raises `ValueError('Checkpoint was created for different inputs or model settings...')` on any mismatch — it never silently serves a stale result. It goes further than a config-hash: `_load_checkpoint` (processor.py:343) also checks each stored row's `input` text against the live `items[idx]` byte-for-byte and raises if they diverge, before that row is ever reused. README line 75, verified verbatim: 'Reusing data.ckpt with another input, model, prompt, or sampling config fails fast.' This is exactly PASS_REPLAY's shape — a stored result is only replayed (no request re-sent) when hash and byte-identity checks both pass — and a stronger instance than the register's existing PASS_REPLAY precedent (id 258, bespokelabs/curator), which guarantees byte-identity only by re-reading the same on-disk file, with no explicit hash. Two scope caveats, neither disqualifying: (1) BatchLLM drives concurrent chat-completions calls to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, not the provider's async Batches/Message-Batches job-submission API — 'batch' means 'a batch of rows BatchLLM processes,' not the dedicated Batches endpoint id 258 wraps. (2) The repo carries 4 GitHub stars (confirmed via `gh api repos/he-yufeng/BatchLLM`, 2026-08-20). Per the register's 2026-08-20 advocate pass, which reinstated ids 16 and 18 after downloading and reading their code directly ('structural arguments, not the tools' say-so... obscurity is not a verdict'), low reach does not cap the verdict once the mechanism is verified in source — it's recorded here as a reach caveat, not a downgrade.
entry.savings: UNQUANTIFIED — avoids re-billing rows already completed before a crash/interrupt; magnitude scales with how much of a run had finished when it stopped (same shape as the register's id 258, no fixed percentage published for either).

Confirmed the SHA-256 fingerprint construction (processor.py:307-320), the fingerprint check on checkpoint load (processor.py:358-366), and the per-row byte-identical input check (processor.py:343) directly in source. Star count (4) confirmed via `gh api repos/he-yufeng/BatchLLM`.

The disqualifying find: `fields` — the full CSV row / JSONL object that documented "Multi-field templates" (README:171-182, with BatchLLM's own worked example: `-t "Translate this review to {language}, then summarize it in one line: {text}"`) expose to the prompt template as `{column}` — is in neither the fingerprint payload (307-320 hashes only `items`, the input-column text) nor the per-row checkpoint check (343 compares stored `input` only against `items[idx]`). Edit the `language` column's values between runs, keep `text` (the input_column) and every BatchConfig field identical, resume with the same `--checkpoint`: fingerprint matches, per-row byte check matches, and the row replays the OLD translation's output against what is now a differently-constructed prompt — no ValueError, no warning, same code path the entry cites as airtight. That falsifies "it never silently serves a stale result" as written, and falsifies the trap's explicit "no silent gap there" — the gap isn't in sampling params, it's in the template-variable surface, and it's a first-class documented feature, not an obscure corner. The core hash+byte mechanism is real and does gate replay correctly for single-column (`{input}`-only) prompts, which keeps this at PASS_REPLAY rather than a lower class — but the entry needs the trap rewritten around the actual gap (multi-field templates, not api_key) before it can stand as verified, and "never silently serves a stale result" needs scoping to "for prompts that reference only {input}."

Refuter #2, MECHANISM lens: does not survive. Re-fetched processor.py and README.md at commit 1d787b3c8ceac97677a1269e526efb7028e3a2a2 (gh api confirms sha, date, 4 stars) — every quote and line number the entry cites checks out verbatim (control phrase confirmed present verbatim: README's "Reusing data.ckpt with another input, model, prompt, or sampling config fails fast"). But the entry verified only a subset of what actually reaches the model. _build_messages (processor.py:181) builds the outbound prompt via `_render_template(self.config.prompt_template, input_text, fields)`, and _render_template (processor.py:56-68) substitutes every other CSV column / JSONL field into `{column}` placeholders — this is BatchLLM's own headlined "Multi-field templates" feature (README:43, 171-181; e.g. `-t "Translate this review to {language}, then summarize it in one line: {text}"`), not an obscure edge case. `fields` is absent from `_make_checkpoint_fingerprint`'s hash (processor.py:307-320, which hashes only items/model/system_prompt/prompt_template/max_tokens/temperature/base_url/max_retries/timeout), is never persisted to the checkpoint file at all (`_save_checkpoint`, processor.py:399-421, writes only index/input/output/error/error_type/tokens_in/tokens_out/latency_ms), and is not covered by the per-row load check (processor.py:343 compares only `data.get("input","") != items[idx]`, i.e. the raw input-column text, never the rendered prompt). Concrete failure: checkpoint a multi-field run, interrupt it, edit only the `language` (or any non-input) column for an already-completed row, resume with the same `--checkpoint` — fingerprint matches, per-row input matches, and the stale translation is replayed verbatim; the row the model would actually read on a fresh call is never sent. This is structurally the same defect this same register already downgraded at id 259 (bespokelabs/curator, sweep-14): a hash over a declared subset of the generative inputs ("recipe") rather than the full rendered request, with an untracked remainder free to drift the real outbound content while the guard reports a clean match. BatchLLM's case is if anything more clear-cut than curator's — id 259 needed a non-pure-function hypothesis to trigger; this needs only normal use of a documented, first-class feature plus a checkpoint resume. The submitted entry's own "trap" section caught the narrower api_key exclusion but missed this larger, code-confirmed gap entirely. Per the id 259 precedent in this register, a fingerprint/replay guard that verifiably checks a proxy for the request rather than the request's actual content does not meet PASS_REPLAY's bar — downgrading PASS_REPLAY -> FAIL.
